note: validateRegistration(d) returns only { readinessClass, daysSinceBirth, lateRegistration, missingItemCount } - no rules array and no flags - so this is a SPLIT engine: the oracle pins detectFlaggedIssues(state) as expected.flaggedIssues with flagsArgs ["state"], mirroring form-app.js's `detectFlaggedIssues(state)`. Classification is first-match: outOfScopeReason (stillbirth yes, or a birth country other than england/wales) -> 'out-of-scope'; any missing required item or date inconsistency -> 'incomplete'; any evidence gap (informant problem, paternity route or evidence, insufficient identity evidence, non-original documents, more than 365 days) -> 'needs-additional-evidence'; else 'ready-to-submit'. Days are whole days from dateOfBirth to registrationDate (UTC); the 42-day period, the 35-day warning and the 365-day limit are in rules.js. A late registration of 43 to 365 days raises a flag but does not by itself block ready-to-submit. The 'timestamp' key is added by form-app.js, not the grader. Regenerate expected with: bin/test-personas united-kingdom-birth-registration --update

flaggedIssues.description: The child's personal child health record (red book) will not be brought; some registrars ask to see it.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Bring the red book if you have it.

flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Complete the missing items before attending the register office; the registrar needs them to make the entry.

flaggedIssues.description: Certificates are ordered but no delivery address is given.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Enter the postal address the certificates should be sent to.

personas.name: Needs evidence: unmarried father named with no valid basis
personas.description: Unmarried parents, father included, but the basis is none and the mother registers alone. Expect needs-additional-evidence with the paternity-route flag.

flaggedIssues.description: The stated basis cannot be used to record the second parent for these parents.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Unmarried parents: register together, bring a signed statutory declaration of parentage, or bring a court document giving parental responsibility. A male couple needs a parental order.

personas.name: Needs evidence: 63 days after birth, one secondary document, photocopies
personas.description: Registration 63 days after the birth; only one secondary identity document and not originals. Expect needs-additional-evidence, late registration yes, with the late, identity-evidence and originals flags.

child.placeOfBirth: Royal Berkshire Hospital, London Road, Reading

flaggedIssues.description: Registration is 63 days after the birth; a birth in England and Wales must be registered within 42 days.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Register without further delay and tell the registrar why the birth was not registered in time.

flaggedIssues.description: No acceptable identity evidence is held: one accepted document (for example a passport or photocard driving licence), or two from the secondary list, is needed.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Gather one accepted identity document, or two secondary documents such as a utility bill and a bank statement, showing your name.

flaggedIssues.description: The identity documents must be originals; photocopies are not accepted.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Bring the original documents to the register office.

personas.name: Out of scope: birth in Scotland
